ideas.description: Exploit: spend the tip's margin on epochs. Start from tip E028 (commit 88b116f). First confirm in the code that it is the Muon line: Muon lr 0.24 / momentum 0.6 on block convs, fused into the graphed step, 128/256/704, first 50% of steps at 24 px with antialias, translate 2, LS 0.1, alternating flip, batch 2048, 9.5 ep, fused SGD+Lookahead on the rest. Change only the epoch count, from 9.5 to 8.75. Rescale the LR, Lookahead and Muon schedules to the new step count so they still anneal fully, keep the 24 px phase at the first 50% of steps, and recapture graphs in build if the step count is baked in. Report per-seed accuracy. If the 3-seed margin over 0.753 is under 0.3 pp, rerun once and pool before promoting (H1.1.3 rule). This also measures the Muon slope below 9.5 ep: E027 gave 0.29 pp/ep for 11 to 9.5.
ideas.expected: Time about 5.38-5.45 s (-7 to -8% vs 5.84 s). Accuracy -0.2 to -0.4 pp, to about 0.753-0.756. If feasible, it is a new best, and the next step is 8.0 ep. If accuracy lands at 0.750-0.753, the Muon curve steepens below 9.5 ep (concave, as SGD's did), so the epoch lever is nearly spent and margin must come from N3/N6-type levers. Below 0.750 means a knee, not a slope.

ideas.description: Exploit throughput on the batch axis (E024: 1024 to 1536 gave -3.1%; E028: 1536 to 2048 gave -3.9%, both with accuracy flat). On tip E028, change only the batch size, from 2048 to 3072. Hold the per-example LR and wd fixed for the SGD-trained parameters (per-step LR x1.5). Treat the Muon lr exactly as E028's 1536-to-2048 change did (check the commit and use the same convention). Tie warmup/decay, Lookahead and Muon schedules to the new step count, recapture both resolution graphs in build, and handle the last partial batch the same way as now. Report per-seed accuracy and the total step count (about 155).
ideas.expected: Time -2 to -5%, to about 5.55-5.70 s, because Muon's NS cost and the other fixed per-step overheads spread over ~1/3 fewer steps. Accuracy -0.1 to -0.5 pp: at ~16 steps per epoch the sample-limited assumption may break. Feasible with a drop <= 0.2 pp makes this a new best and the default for the epoch-cut line. A drop >= 0.4 pp means the run has become step-limited near ~150 steps, which closes the batch axis at 2048.

ideas.description: Margin builder (rewrite of I041 onto the current tip). Muon lr 0.24 / momentum 0.6 come from airbench94_muon's CIFAR-10 37-to-10-epoch setting at batch 2000. D007 (C0053/C0056/C0065) says shorter horizons favor different step sizes, and Muon tolerates larger lr. On tip E028 (9.5 ep, batch 2048), change only the Muon peak lr, from 0.24 to 0.32: same schedule shape, same momentum, SGD groups unchanged. The precomputed GPU LR table changes; nothing else does.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (+/-0.03 s). Accuracy -0.3 to +0.35 pp, direction uncertain. A gain >= 0.25 pp is worth roughly 0.8 epoch at Muon's ~0.3 pp/epoch, about 0.5 s, so it is spent on the epoch cut next, followed by momentum 0.5. A loss >= 0.25 pp puts the optimum at or below 0.24 and closes Muon lr tuning.

ideas.description: Crux test: is resize still the cheaper lever now that Muon flattened the epoch curve? Under SGD, resize cost ~0.4 pp/s and epochs ~0.75 pp/s, so resize won. Under Muon, epochs cost ~0.31 pp/s (E027), and resize at 75% cost ~1-1.8 pp/s (E029). The marginal resize rate near 50% under Muon is unmeasured. On tip E028, change only the 24 px fraction, from the first 50% to the first 40% of steps (same antialiased bilinear downsample, schedules tied to step count, both shapes still graphed in build). Report per-seed accuracy.
ideas.expected: Time +0.15 to +0.22 s (about 23 more steps at 32 px instead of 24 px, ~9 ms each). Accuracy +0.05 to +0.35 pp. The rate in pp gained per second added decides the next move. If it is > ~0.45 pp/s, beating the ~0.31 pp/s epoch rate, then under Muon less resize plus fewer epochs is the faster frontier, and a 40%/8.5-ep combo is next. If it is <= 0.3 pp/s, 50% stays and margin goes to epochs. Not expected to improve time by itself.

ideas.description: Muon x augmentation crux (rewrite of I040 onto the current tip; D007: C0074/C0075/C0077 say Muon gains more than SGD from stronger augmentation and suffers late spectral collapse with weak augmentation). H4.1's 'weaker is better at ~10 ep' result (E011: translate 2 gave +0.35 pp) was measured under SGD. On tip E028, change only the translate amplitude, from 2 px back to 4 px, in both resolution phases (reflect padding as now). Everything else is fixed.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged. Accuracy -0.4 to +0.3 pp. The committee is split (disagreement 0.79), and the SGD prior points down. A gain >= 0.25 pp means the optimizer flips the regularization optimum: H4.1 must be re-measured on Muon (cutout 8 next), and the margin goes to epochs. A loss >= 0.25 pp means the SGD optimum carries over, and augmentation stays closed on the Muon line.

ideas.description: Explore a schedule component that may be redundant under Muon. airbench94_muon trains without the SGD-era Lookahead, and orthogonalized updates already damp step noise. Lookahead may now only slow late progress at 9.5 ep. On tip E028, change only one thing: remove Lookahead (no slow weights, no _foreach_lerp_ sync) for all parameter groups. Keep the LR/Muon schedules and everything else unchanged, recapture graphs in build, and keep prepare resetting all remaining state.
ideas.expected: Time -0.02 to -0.06 s (one fewer foreach pass per sync step). Accuracy -0.5 to +0.25 pp, direction uncertain. If accuracy is within +/-0.15 pp, keep the removal: it is simpler and slightly faster. A gain >= 0.25 pp means Lookahead was fighting Muon and frees margin for epochs. A loss >= 0.3 pp confirms Lookahead is still a sample-efficiency lever under Muon, and H4.5 then moves to its cadence and alpha.

drop.reason: Its base, the I032/E025 Muon base, is superseded by tip E028 (9.5 ep, batch 2048). It is rewritten as a new idea on E028 that tests the same Muon x augmentation crux.
Its base, the I032/E025 Muon base at 11 ep, is superseded by tip E028. It is rewritten as a new idea on E028 at the current horizon, which is the horizon the lr question is about.

It measures the noise floor on E024, which is no longer the tip. E028 carries a +0.44 pp margin, and the rerun-and-pool rule is built into the new epoch-cut idea instead. Spending two runs on a stale SGD recipe gives little information.

The depth-vs-epochs test sits on the superseded SGD tip E024. Under Muon the epoch slope is different (~0.29 pp/ep), so an SGD answer would not transfer. It has the lowest priority and most members forecast not-improved.

structured_output.summary: The tip is E028 (0.7574 at 5.84 s): Muon on the block convs, 9.5 epochs, batch 2048, 50% of steps at 24 px. Muon changed the exchange rates. Cutting epochs now costs about 0.31 pp/s (E027), cheaper than resize under SGD, and the 75% resize run collapsed (E029), so the resize/epoch trade has flipped and needs re-measuring. New queue, every idea on the E028 tip: (1) priority 5: cut epochs to 8.75, with the rerun-and-pool rule if the margin is thin. (2) priority 4: batch 3072, the third step on the batch axis, which gave -3 to -4% per step so far. (3) priority 3: Muon lr 0.32 to build margin. (4) priority 3: cut the 24 px fraction to 40%; the measured rate decides whether less resize plus fewer epochs beats the current split under Muon. (5) priority 2: translate 4, the Muon x augmentation crux the committee is split on. (6) priority 2: remove Lookahead, which may be redundant with Muon. Dropped: I040 and I041, rewritten onto E028; I042 and I043, which sit on the stale SGD E024 base. I038 (whole-run graph) is still running on E024; if it is kept, port it to E028.
